own_solution.law: Bernoulli + continuity for a horizontal Venturi with manometer: dp = (rho_m - rho) g h; Q = A2 sqrt(2 dp / (rho (1 - (A2/A1)^2)))
assumptions: hydrostatic manometer lines filled with flowing liquid

notes: dp = 12600*9.8*0.12 = 14817.6 Pa; A2 = pi*0.025^2 = 1.9635e-3 m^2; 1 - (A2/A1)^2 = 15/16; v2 = sqrt(2*14817.6/1000/(15/16)) = 5.6224 m/s; Q = 0.011040 m^3/s. With U-tube liquid 2500 kg/m^3 and the same 12 cm reading: dp = 1764 Pa, v2 = 1.9399 m/s, Q = 0.0038090 m^3/s. Absolute pressure 240 kPa: only the difference matters (throat pressure about 225 kPa, no cavitation); pipe height: both tappings at same elevation, so z cancels in Bernoulli. These could also be classed K (cavitation) or D respectively; I chose C. Variants: 2500 kg/m^3 consistent across U-tube/barometer/earlier-run sentences; T90FF/T5A70 carry no number (numeral-free); 240 kPa and 2.1 m pairs differ only in wording.
